ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given, as shown in the figure, the graph of a linear function passes through points $P(3, 2)$ and $B(0, -2)$, and intersects the x-axis at point $A$. What is the analytical expression of the linear function?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the linear function be $y=kx+b$. Substituting points $P(3,2)$ and $B(0, -2)$ into $y=kx+b$, we get
\[
\begin{cases}
3k+b=2\\
b=-2
\end{cases}
\]
Solving these equations, we obtain
\[
\begin{cases}
k=\frac{4}{3}\\
b=-2
\end{cases}
\]
$\therefore$ The equation of the linear function is $\boxed{y=\frac{4}{3}x-2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows coordinate axes with a straight line rising from lower left to upper right. The line meets the y-axis below the origin at B, meets the x-axis at A, and contains point P in the first quadrant. Reasoning: From the text, B=(0,-2) and P=(3,2). The rise from B to P is 2-(-2)=4, and the run is 3-0=3, so the slope is 4/3. Since B has y-value -2, rising to the x-axis y=0 requires a rise of 2. With slope 4/3, the corresponding run is 2/(4/3)=3/2, so A=(3/2,0). Using intercept form with x-intercept 3/2 and y-intercept -2 gives x/(3/2)+y/(-2)=1. Simplifying: (2/3)x - y/2 = 1, so multiplying by 2 gives (4/3)x - y = 2, hence y=(4/3)x-2.
